Halloween (24 Oct to 1 Nov): Magic Ink Pot sensory trail in the House 11:00–16:00 (ground floor only, decorated) and Frightful Fernery outdoor trail 10:00–17:00; both free with admission, no booking.

Quieter, calmer timeslots for children who find busy or loud places hard. Wheelchair and pram friendly; outdoors, so wellies recommended. Carer tickets £2.50 (phone 028 9756 6100). Book the ASD/Quiet timeslot on the Ticketsolve page.

events.name: The O2 Belfast arena (Belfast Giants games and family shows) with sensory bags
events.description: Free sensory bags at the arena's concierge desk for anyone who finds the noise and crowds hard: ear defenders, fidget toys, cue cards, a weighted lap pad and a wobble cushion (leave ID as a deposit). You can ask for a familiarisation visit on a non-event day through the venue's Contact Us page, and an Essential Companion ticket can be free. Belfast Giants also made a BBC Bitesize 'Let's Go Out!' sensory story video to help children prepare for a game night. Ice hockey and arena shows are loud, so ear defenders are a must.
events.recurring: On event days (Giants home games and family shows)
events.time: Box office opens 1 hour before doors
events.venue: The O2 Belfast (formerly SSE Arena), Odyssey, Queen's Quay
events.price: Event ticket; sensory bag free; Essential Companion ticket may be free

events.name: Larne FC home games with sensory bags (Inver Park)
events.description: Staff and volunteers are CALM-trained, and sensory bags with ear defenders and fidget toys are available at every home game for children with autism. Book at least 24 hours ahead by emailing samneill@larnefc.com, then collect from the ticket office. A free personal assistant ticket may be available.
events.price: Match ticket; sensory bag free (book 24h ahead)

events.name: Ballymoney Halloween Quiet Time (additional needs)
events.description: Causeway Coast & Glens Council's Ballymoney Halloween night opens with an hour of Quiet Time for people with additional needs, with reduced noise and lighting. It includes the amusements, Eurekaseekers, Ray Bubbles, chocolate-apple decorating and a balloon modeller. The busy main event follows from 6:30pm (fireworks 8:30pm). Entry is free; rides are paid. Pre-bookable disabled parking and a Mobile Accessible Changing Unit are available (parking: Bushmills Visitor Information Centre, 028 2073 0390).

events.name: Ballycastle Halloween Quiet Time (additional needs)
events.description: Causeway Coast & Glens Council's Ballycastle Halloween night has an hour of Quiet Time for people with additional needs on the Seafront, with creepy critters, a circus workshop, Ray Bubbles and quieter amusements. The full event follows from 6:30pm (fireworks 8:30pm). Entry is free; rides are paid. A Mobile Accessible Changing Unit is on the Seafront.

events.name: Ready Steady Gym at Valdez Gymnastics (extra-support class)
events.description: A 45-minute structured gymnastics class for primary-school-age children who need extra support, with two coaches to six children, sensory equipment and apparatus matched to each child's development. Entry is after an assessment and chat with the parent, so contact the club first. Valdez is an all-inclusive club affiliated with Special Olympics Ireland.
events.venue: Valdez Gymnastics, Unit 12A Woodside Industrial Estate, Woodside Road

events.name: The Snowman Family Concert (relaxed performance)
events.description: Ulster Orchestra plays Howard Blake's score live to The Snowman film. Both shows are relaxed and signed: noise and movement are fine, you can come and go during the show, there's a chill-out space on level one, and noise-cancelling headphones are welcome. Sound and lighting are not turned down, apart from slight dimming during the film.

events.name: Magic and Mistletoe Christmas Quiet Sessions (additional needs)
events.description: Quiet sessions of Magheramorne Estate's outdoor Christmas trail for children with additional needs, with low audio and restricted guest numbers. Includes meeting Father Christmas, farm animals, marshmallow toasting and all food. Gravel paths with slopes and steps. The 2026 event is showing as sold out, so watch for swaps or returns.

events.name: Abbey Allsorts Special Needs Club (children with additional needs + siblings)
events.description: Parent-run charity club in Newtownabbey for children with disabilities and their brothers and sisters: arts and crafts, singing and dancing, messy play, children's entertainers and family games. Sensory and Makaton friendly, with a hoist and changing bench available. Parents or carers stay with their children. Saturday sessions are announced on their Facebook page, and Listening Ear Newtownabbey (Rathcoole) also lists an evening session on the last Tuesday of each month, 6:30 to 8pm. Contact abbeyallsorts@mail.com or 07754 678497 to check the next date.
events.recurring: Saturdays as announced on Facebook; also last Tuesday of each month

events.name: Active & Able Halloween Camp (disabled children 5–15), Avoniel
events.description: Three-afternoon Halloween sports camp made specially for children aged 5 to 15 with learning or physical disabilities. events.name: The Smeds and the Smoos relaxed screening (Cinemagic)
events.description: A short 25-minute relaxed screening of the animated story about two young aliens from rival families, made for neurodiverse audiences and children with sensory sensitivities. The house lights stay dimly lit, the sound is turned down, seating is limited for extra space, and children can move around, make noise, or come and go at any time. Cert U. Every attendee needs a ticket except under-2s on a lap; carers get the concession price.
events.venue: Ulster Museum Lecture Theatre, Botanic Gardens, BT9 5AB

events.name: The Junction Pumpkin Patch: Sensory Sessions
events.description: Dedicated sensory sessions of The Junction's Halloween pumpkin patch, run every open day. They are quieter, with reduced numbers and trained staff on hand. Children push a mini wheelbarrow round the patch, pick a pumpkin, then decorate it at the decorating station with paints, brushes and stickers (no carving) and take it home. Each session lasts about 45 minutes. Accompanying adults need a free ticket (max 2 adults per child). Book the 'Pumpkin Patch - Sensory Sessions' listing, not the general one. Closed Monday 26 and Tuesday 27 October.
events.recurring: Daily 24–31 Oct except Mon 26 & Tue 27 Oct
events.venue: The Junction Retail & Leisure Park, 111 Ballymena Road, BT41 4LL
events.price: £8 per child (incl. pumpkin and decorating); adults free ticket

events.name: The Ark Open Farm Halloween Pumpkin Patch: Quiet Session
events.description: A quiet session of The Ark's Halloween experience especially for families with children with additional support needs, held before the farm opens fully at 10am. Pick a pumpkin with a wheelbarrow (staff carve it for you), slime making, marshmallow toasting, Halloween trail and Fairytale Forest, barrel ride, animals and play areas. Carer tickets £3; Essential Companion tickets £3 for Access Card holders. Under-1s free. £1 booking fee.
events.price: Child £18 (incl. pumpkin), toddler £8, adult £16–19, carer £3; family of 4 £64

events.name: Relaxed Screening: Toy Story 5
events.description: Relaxed cinema screening run by Newcastle Community Cinema with Autism Support Kilkeel (ASK) and ADHD Hub, for neurodiverse people and their families. Softer sound, lower lighting and a relaxed atmosphere where you can move around, make noise or take a break. Everyone welcome; tickets just £3 per person, book online through TicketSource. Film: Toy Story 5 (PG, 102 min).
events.venue: Newcastle Community Cinema, St Mary's Hall, Main Street

events.name: Larne YMCA Autism Support Programme (ASP) Saturday club
events.description: Weekly social and play club at Larne YMCA set up for children aged 4+ with autism (or waiting on a diagnosis). Small groups with games in the hall, arts and crafts, football, cooking, park trips and seasonal Halloween and Christmas fun, plus a quiet chill-out room for sensory time and calming down. It's popular and sometimes has a waiting list, so contact Leanne Doherty (leanne@larneymca.org) or call 028 2827 9331 (option 1) to ask about a place before going.
events.recurring: Weekly on Saturdays (term time; check for closures)

events.name: National Autistic Society Dad's Stay and Play
events.description: A two-hour shared play group run by the National Autistic Society NI for dads and their autistic children of primary school age who have complex support needs. Children can use the centre's sensory equipment and activities while National Autistic Society staff support the dads. You need to contact them first to get a place: email Joanne.Keown@nas.org.uk.
events.venue: National Autistic Society NI Autism Centre, Eastbank House, 3 Eastbank Road, Carryduff, BT8 8BD (confirm when you contact them)

events.name: Santa at The Wee Village (calm, child-led Santa visit)
events.description: Not a dedicated SEN session, but built to be low-pressure: 90 minutes of play in a countryside role-play village (Gruffalo theme this year), and Santa sits by the tree so children can go to him whenever they're ready, or not at all. There are no queues and no rush. Each child gets a personalised gift bag, a festive snack and a drink. The same venue runs inclusive additional-needs sessions with the music off and lower lighting, so it's worth asking about a quieter slot when you book. Dates are limited.
events.recurring: Selected dates over Christmas 2026 (on sale now; check availability)
events.venue: The Wee Village, 29B Deer Park Road, Ballyclare, BT39 0RH

events.name: WAVE Ballyclare monthly group for people with special needs (all ages, Makaton-trained leaders)
events.description: A relaxed, cross-church monthly gathering for children and adults with special needs or disabilities, with their parents and carers. It uses arts and crafts, drama and storytelling rather than talking, and the leaders (several are teachers) are trained in Makaton, which suits a non-verbal child. Parents can chat over a cup of tea. It is a Christian group with a short faith element. Still listed as running by the WAVE network; check the group's Facebook page or the church before your first visit. Next date should be Sunday 25 October.
events.venue: Ballyclare Presbyterian Church, 2 Foundry Lane, Ballyclare, BT39 9BQ

events.name: Kidz Quest Connect: additional-needs children's group, Scrabo Hall (ages 4–11)
events.description: A small-group session for children aged 4 to 11 with additional needs who can't manage the mainstream children's programme, whether because of sensory, learning or behavioural difficulties. Numbers are kept small and sensory stimulation is turned down, and activities are pitched to each child. Experienced volunteers run a special-needs session on Sunday mornings during the church's family service. It's a church group with simple Bible stories. Get in touch through their contact page before going so they can plan for your child.
events.venue: Scrabo Hall, 143–161 Mill Street, Newtownards, BT23 4LN

events.name: Northern Ireland football at Windsor Park with a sensory Quiet Room
events.description: The national stadium has a soundproofed Quiet Room in the family stand, set up with the National Autistic Society: soft floor, comfy seats, calm LED lighting, sensory toys, its own accessible toilet and a full view of the pitch. It takes up to 5 people, with one free essential companion ticket and junior prices for children. There is also a Quiet Seating area. Request it through the Irish FA accessible ticket form when tickets for a men's or women's home international go on sale; places are first come, first served. Questions to dao@irishfa.com.
events.recurring: Northern Ireland men's and women's home internationals
events.venue: National Football Stadium at Windsor Park, Donegall Avenue, Belfast
events.price: Normal adult/junior match prices; one essential companion free

events.name: Carryduff All Stars: Gaelic games for children with additional needs (age 5+)

Sessions are gentle exercise, simple games and ball skills, with the focus on fun and joining in at the child's own pace in a safe, friendly setting, and the team also goes to Ulster GAA For All festival days. About 150 people take part. The club doesn't publish the session day online, so email Maria at healthandwellbeing@carryduffgac.com to ask about times and a place before going.

events.name: The People's Panto: Pinocchio (ASD friendly performance)
events.description: Brassneck Theatre Company's community Christmas panto in west Belfast has one ASD friendly performance of Pinocchio this year. The show runs about 1 hour 50 minutes including an interval, so it's a long sit for a 5 or 6 year old. Seating is unreserved, but seats can be held for people with a disability if you tell Brassneck what you need when booking (email finn@brassnecktheatrecompany.com). Children under 12 must come with an adult, and tickets can't be refunded.
events.venue: St Comgall's, 2 Divis Street / Falls Road, Belfast, BT12 4AQ

events.name: Tumble Circus Winter Circus (relaxed performance)
events.description: Belfast's Christmas circus in a heated Big Top in the Cathedral Quarter has one relaxed show this year, for people with autism, a learning disability or sensory and communication needs. Noise and moving about are fine, light and sound effects are toned down, there's extra seating space and an accessible portable toilet on site. Expect aerialists, juggling, acrobatics and comedy, all ages welcome. The show is about 70 minutes with no interval. Doors open 4:45pm. Carers get a free ticket (email bookings@tumblecircus.com), and it's worth giving advance notice of specific needs when booking. Winter Circus sells out every year, so book early.
events.venue: Tumble Circus Big Top, Writers' Square, Donegall Street, Belfast, BT1 2HB

events.name: Let's Play playgroup for children with additional needs, Rosstulla School (ages 0–6)
events.description: A weekly play session at Rosstulla special school in Jordanstown for children up to 6 with additional needs, with a parent or carer joining in. It's play-based and led by the school's experienced SEN staff in the nursery classroom, so it's a calm, understanding space, and a chance to meet other parents of children with additional needs. It runs on Wednesday afternoons, so it suits days your child is off school or finishes early. The page doesn't say whether it runs during school holidays or whether you need to book, so ring the school on 028 9086 2743 before going.

events.name: SEN Space Family Sessions (monthly Sunday, additional needs)
events.description: A Sunday morning session once a month at SEN Space, a charity centre in Dunmurry built for children with additional needs. The whole family can use the sensory rooms, arts and crafts, indoor and outdoor play areas and an acre of safe, enclosed garden, and meet the staff and other families in the same position. They cap the number of families so it doesn't get overwhelming, and all ages are welcome, including siblings. Upcoming dates are Sun 22 Nov, Sun 13 Dec, Sun 17 Jan and Sun 21 Feb, 11am–12:30pm, booked on SEN Space's Eventbrite page (search "Inclusive Play & Family Fun for Children with Additional Needs"), or contact them on 07830 355 003 or info@senspace.org.uk.

events.venue: SEN Space, 4 Thornhill Road, Dunmurry, BT17 9EJ

events.name: Lush Belfast Little Monsters bath bomb workshop (SEN sensory-friendly session)
events.description: A 45-minute Halloween half-term workshop at the Lush shop in Belfast city centre where children make their own pumpkin-themed vegan bath bomb, play a couple of spooky party games and take home a goodie bag. One session is set aside as a SEN sensory-friendly slot: it runs at a more relaxed pace and the music is turned down. Suitable for all ages, so a parent can stay alongside. Worth knowing: the shop and the bath bomb are strongly scented (cinnamon, lime and orange), so it suits children who enjoy smells and messy hands-on play more than those who find scents overwhelming. Book the 10am Thursday slot specifically on the Lush event page.

events.name: White Rise playground, Lagmore (sensory-friendly equipment + communication panel)
events.description: Belfast City Council playground in Lagmore, west Belfast, reopened at Easter 2026 after a full refurbishment. The council says it is designed to be welcoming for all children, including those with sensory processing differences: it has sensory-friendly acoustic (sound-making) play equipment, a communication panel (a picture board a non-verbal child can point at), wheelchair-accessible features, and new safety surfacing and fencing. Free, open daily, no booking. It's a local neighbourhood playground rather than a big destination park.
events.venue: White Rise playground, Lagmore, Belfast BT17

events.name: You2Me Christmas Breakfast & Play (with Santa)

events.price: Inflata 5+ £15.95 (Fri term £11.95) + £1.50 socks; soft play over-4s £8.75–£9.50; bowling child £6.95

events.name: Puffling Percy (children's puppet & live music show)

events.description: Three-day Halloween multi-sports camp (dance, dodgeball, football, team games) run by qualified coaches. Ages 5–11. Book online with a getactiveabc account (add your child as a family member first). Bring a water bottle and snack.
